title: PM 20-minute SDK demo + telemetry checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, PM-facing 20-minute path to: 1) validate that a feature team can run the SDK demo, 2) collect the minimum telemetry we need to evaluate adoption/quality, and 3) provide an observable, repeatable handoff script for a product demo. This is intentionally concise — think: checklist + demo script + minimal telemetry contract.

Audience and context:
- Primary: Product Managers (PMs) and Solutions Engineers running short demos with stakeholders.
- Secondary: Eng-DevEx for troubleshooting and SRE for telemetry wiring.
- This doc assumes the dev team has: a feature branch with a minimal sample app, an API key for the hosted sandbox, and a telemetry tag in their repo.

Success criteria (what PM signs off on after the 20m session):
- Demo app boots within 3 minutes of the environment checklist completing.
- A sample request yields a valid response < 1s median (sandbox expectation).
- Telemetry events for request, latency, and error are visible in the shared dashboard within 5 minutes.
- Prompt-regression smoke: top-3 prompts return expected intent at least 80% of the time (manual check).

Quick prep (5 minutes) — Pre-demo checklist
- Environment: macOS/Linux or Codespace; node 18+/python 3.10+ installed.
- Credentials: PM has a sandbox API key (redwood-sandbox-xxx). Confirm permission tier for the key.
- Repo: clone/checkout the minimal-sample-app branch (link in linked_artifacts).
- Telemetry: ensure the sample app has REDWOOD_TELEM_ENABLED=true and the telemetry tag set (see telemetry contract section).
- Network: confirm outbound to api.redwood.ai and that no corporate proxy blocks streaming ports.

20-minute demo script (timeboxed):
- Minute 0–2: Quick context + goals (PM speaks).
- Minute 2–5: Start app (npm run dev / python demo.py). Narrate what the SDK does and the main integration points.
- Minute 5–10: Run three curated prompts live: one trivial, one edge-case, one domain-specific. Share latency numbers aloud.
  - Prompt A (trivial): "Summarize this sentence in one line."
  - Prompt B (edge): "Given an ambiguous user request, ask a clarifying question."
  - Prompt C (domain): short domain prompt relevant to stakeholder.
- Minute 10–12: Show fallback: turn off network/force error and demonstrate graceful fallback.
- Minute 12–16: Show the console/dashboard: trace for the three requests, latency histogram, error logs, and token cost approximate.
- Minute 16–18: Quick ask: gather stakeholder acceptance and next-step ask (pilot, dedicated capacity, integration).
- Minute 18–20: Wrap + actions. Confirm who picks up follow-ups.

Minimal telemetry contract (what must be emitted by the sample app):
- Names/keys (minimal set):
  - event: sdk.request.sent (string event)
  - event: sdk.request.completed (string event)
  - attribute: request.latency_ms (integer)
  - attribute: request.success (boolean)
  - attribute: request.model (string)
  - attribute: prompt.id (string) — free text id for the prompt template used
  - attribute: error.code (string) if any
- Emission window: events should be visible in the shared devexp dashboard within 5 minutes of occurrence.
- Sampling: for demo/sandbox, send 100% of events. For production, default to 5% unless flagged for debug.

Observability checklist for the PM to verify (during the demo):
- Telemetry event sdk.request.completed appears for each of the three live prompts.
- Latency shown for each request and median under threshold (demo threshold: 1200ms).
- Error sample shows stack or error.code if triggered by the fallback test.
- Token cost estimation displayed (rough per-minute cost line item).

Prompt regression quick-check (manual):
- Bring the three prompts used in the demo into a small test sheet (CSV).
- After the demo, re-run those prompts once via the API and capture outputs.
- Manually confirm intent/critical fields for domain prompt (pass if >=80% matches).
- If a regression is suspected, create ticket: TAG "prompt-regression" with the CSV and a short note.

Failure modes & troubleshooting (fast triage notes):
- App fails to start: check env vars (API key, REDWOOD_TELEM_ENABLED), node/python version, and port collisions.
- Requests time out: check outbound network and sandbox region; try local curl test: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text --header "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"redwood-lite","input":"hi"}'
- No telemetry events: confirm SDK telemetry integration file present, env var set, and local logs for event flush.

Artifacts to create during/after the demo (PM actions):
- Create a one-paragraph pilot ask with target success metrics and estimated monthly tokens.
- If integration goes well: request a dedicated sandbox key (DEV-DEDICATED-REQ) and link to the sample app branch.
- If prompt regression appears: open a Jira ticket with label prompt-regression and attach CSV + expected outcomes.

Notes on security & data handling for PMs (high level):
- Sandbox keys are ephemeral — rotate every 30 days.
- Do not paste PII into demo prompts. If required, anonymize sample records.

Quick example curl (for PM to show a single reproducible call):
- curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions" -H "Authorization: Bearer redwood-sandbox-xxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize: Redwood is a platform for LLM inference."}] }'

Follow-ups & handoff template (short):
- PM creates a follow-up doc with: observed latency, token estimate, stakeholder ask, and recommended rollout path (pilot -> dedicated).
- Assign to: feature-owner + eng-devexp + solutions-eng for next steps.

Appendix: short checklist to paste into calendar invite (one-liner tasks):
- Run app + confirm port up
- Confirm sandbox key present and working (1 sample request)
- Confirm telemetry events appear in dashboard
- Run three live prompts + capture results
- Trigger fallback scenario and show graceful degradation

Open questions (for eng-devexp to resolve before finalizing):
- Should we add an automated prompt-regression harness attached to the demo repo? (proposal: yes, small CSV + CI job)
- What is the canonical dashboard URL for PMs (single sign-on friendly)?
- Can we provide a pre-provisioned ephemeral key generator for PM-run demos?

——
Notes to self: this doc is intentionally concise — follow with a longer "playbook" only if PMs ask for more operational detail. The goal here is predictability and low friction for demo-driven adoption conversations.
